summary.headline: Happy Forgings Q4 FY26 revenue rose 20.4% YoY to Rs.424 crore, with EBITDA margin at 31.5% and FY27 volume growth guided to late-teens.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.424 crore (up 20.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs.133 crore (up 30.4%) at a 31.5% margin, and PAT Rs.84 crore (up 23.6%). FY26 revenue reached Rs.1,546 crore (up 9.8%), with EBITDA of Rs.471 crore (30.4% margin) and PAT of Rs.302 crore (19.5% margin). Management guided to late-teens volume growth in FY27 with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26, and flagged raw material and other manufacturing cost inflation linked to the US-Iran situation, which it is seeking to pass on to OEMs from 1 April. Management stressed a shift toward new PV, industrial and heavy-forging programmes at higher realisations (Rs.340-350/kg vs current Rs.245/kg).

financial_highlights.value: Rs.84 crore (19.7% margin) / Rs.302 crore (19.5% margin)

segments.name: Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: Largest segment at 37% of FY26 revenue; domestic MHCV growth strong, but exports fell single digit for the year and about 25% in Q4. Management expects a market share gain and 35-40% CV growth in FY27.

segments.name: Farm equipment
segments.commentary: 32% of FY26 operating revenue, growing around mid-teens for the company; largely domestic. Market share targeted to rise from about 41% to about 45%.

segments.name: Industrials
segments.commentary: 14% of FY26 operating revenue; domestic grew about 59% and exports fell about 11% for the year (per Q&A). Q4 domestic growth about 32%.

segments.name: Off-highway
segments.commentary: 11% of FY26 revenue; domestic construction equipment sales fell 7% in the industry. Q4 domestic off-highway declined about 6% for the company.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: 6% of FY26 revenue; Q4 domestic PV growth about 35%. A large customer's share rose from 32% to 47%, with one more line added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at late-teens, with EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26 levels.
FY27 capex guided at Rs.450-500 crore; planned capex over next two years about Rs.800 crore including solar.
Forging capacity to rise from 147,000 t to 161,000 t by FY27 and 187,000 t by FY28; machining capacity from 69,000 t to 82,000 t by FY27 and 87,000 t by FY28.
Price hikes of about 3.5-4% sought from customers for non-steel cost inflation from 1 April; management expects confirmation from 70-80% of customers within about 10-15 days.
Captive solar plant of 35 AC MW (Rs.170 crore outlay): partial benefits from FY28, full benefits thereafter.
Rs.950 crore new-business order book to be executed over 2-3 years; Rs.250 crore of it is heavy data-centre forgings (700 kg-1.8 t).
capex_capacity: Forging capacity 147,000 t last year; 10,000 t forging line commissioned in Q4 FY26; 4,000 t press expected in H1 FY27 for passenger car programs.
Machining capacity expanded to 68,000 t in FY26, including 9,800 t added in Q3 FY26.
Large capex for data-centre and heavy-engine forgings to complete by end FY27; trials early FY28 and revenue from Q2-Q3 FY28 at Rs.800-1,000/kg realisation.
Wind pinion shaft capex expected to start from Q2 FY27; solar plant generation to begin from Q4 FY27 with 70-80% benefit next year.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand supported by GST rationalisation, infrastructure spending and fleet utilisation; domestic tractor industry strong in FY26; export CV, farm and off-highway markets weak.
Management says Rs.140 crore of new business won in the last four months (industrials and PV), and new order book for Q4 about Rs.150 crore per annum.
Realisation on new order book Rs.340-350/kg versus current Rs.245/kg; management attributes margin gains to higher-precision, higher-value programs.
Steel is a pass-through: domestic with one-month lag, exports with one-quarter lag. Fuel is about 1% of cost (up 30-40%); power about 7% of cost with no hike.
Crank shaft share about 50% of business in FY25 and FY26, expected to reach 58-60% by FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What new businesses and product mix shift are planned over the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites Rs.950 crore new-business order book (Rs.250 crore heavy data-centre). Target mix: CV about 27% (from 37%), industrials 30-31% (from 11%), PV about 10% (from 6%). Typical product price moving from about Rs.60,000 to about Rs.25 lakh, heaviest part from 200 kg to 2 t.

qa_highlights.question: How much price hike is being sought from customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel is passed through. Besides steel, about 3.5-4% selling price increase sought for freight, carbide and packaging cost inflation (2-2.5% of revenue). Confirmations received from some OEMs, hoped for from 1 April.

qa_highlights.question: Can the data-centre capacity be fast-tracked given the AI infrastructure boom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says customers are building infrastructure; the company expects infrastructure ready by Q4 FY27, with 6-9 months development lead time before revenue. Some OEMs have funded tooling, which management cites as commitment.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving gross margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: PV, industrial and some new CV programs at higher realisation. The Rs.950 crore order book realises Rs.340-350/kg versus about Rs.245/kg now. Raw material prices fell about 6% this year while realisation held.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 volume growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CV volumes expected to rise 35-40% on market-share gains (32% to 42% in MHCV). Farm share expected to rise from 41% to about 45%. FADA April data showed tractors up 23% and MHCV up about 15%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects European CV demand to grow single digit; North America ramp-up from Q2 FY27 for passenger cars, with an EV program from FY28 and a European industrial order starting FY29.

risks_watch: Raw material and fuel inflation linked to the US-Iran situation; pass-through depends on OEM confirmations and PO amendments.
Export CV and off-highway weakness in North America and Europe; Q4 CV exports fell about 25%.
Data-centre and heavy-forging revenue depends on infrastructure readiness by customers, with revenue not expected until Q3 FY28.
Other income fell to Rs.6 crore in Q4 (from Rs.10 crore) with about Rs.4.5 crore FX loss.
Management declined to give a specific FY28 volume target; margin uplift from new order mix is medium-term.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on FY27 growth, new orders and margins, but guarded on cost recovery, which is still under negotiation with customers. Management was evasive on specific FY28 volume targets and on fast-tracking the data-centre timeline.
key_quotes: So put together, all this, we see a market share gain starting from this year and also the new segmental growth on industrial as well as EV will be a major growth driver going forward for next 2 to 3 years.
Higher realizations that we are working more towards the technology components and it's a higher precision requirement.
Our strong balance sheet and cash generation capacities provide us significant headroom to fund our growth without relying excessively on external capital.
